dedupe_keys.name: rimini optimised seawater protection plan against sewage overflows climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Rimini's Optimised Seawater Protection Plan (PSBO), adopted in 2013 because heavy rain overflowed the combined sewers, flooded streets and discharged diluted wastewater into the sea, forcing bathing bans. Most of the city's combined sewer was replaced by a separate system; where that was impossible, pumping and storage were added, including an underground runoff storage plant in operation since 2020, and the treatment plant was upgraded. ARPAE modelled the hydraulic system and set the design level at a 1-in-50-year event. Costs were about 200 million euros by late 2023, split between the municipality, the utility and water tariffs. Coverage is the city of Rimini. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2024 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the waterfront works run to 2026, and diluted wastewater is still released to sea when storage is full. Simulation uses: sewer separation and storage sizing for overflow and flood adaptation. Related records: Philadelphia's Green City, Clean Waters (case_study-philadelphia-green-city-clean-waters).
